items.title: Age-specific excess mortality patterns and transmissibility during the 1889–1890 influenza pandemic in Madrid, Spain
items.note: In Madrid’s first wave, people aged 70 and over had the highest excess respiratory death rate and children aged 5–14 the lowest.

items.title: Identifying signature features of epidemic diseases from 19th century all-cause mortality data
items.note: Danish parish burials show a nationwide surge in 1891–92, with the greatest burden among people aged 60 and over.

items.title: The health and demographic impacts of the “Russian flu” pandemic in Switzerland in 1889/1890 and in the years thereafter
items.note: Uses Swiss death and population records to examine age, place and the timing of mortality.
